clue.text: Sent his letter, prepared to engage in controversy

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready or worked up, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone posts a letter, ready to stir up an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges the thirteen letters of SENT HIS LETTER. The lists were the fenced arena of a medieval tournament, hence the idiom for joining a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to enter the arena of a jousting tournament, figuratively joining an argument or contest.

clue.text: Without entering mountainous area Jack is in high fashion

parts.note: EX is a Latin-derived prefix and preposition meaning without, as in ex dividend

indicators.note: one piece going into another shows the pair placed inside the hilly word

parts.note: mountainous country is hilly
a jack (jack tar) is a sailor, and a rating is an ordinary sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor who stays out of the mountains is somehow in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' sends the area and the sailor inside the hilly word. Jack looks like a name but is the sailor; 'is' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in an exciting, spirit-lifting manner, which is a high-spirited fashion of doing things.

clue.text: Try to get a lift in Northumberland

indicators.note: the word in shows the answer sits within the letters of the county name

explanation.surface: A hitch-hiker attempts to get a ride somewhere in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Northumberland is England's northernmost county. 'in' signals the five letters lying inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitch-hikers stick out a digit at passing cars, so the verb means to beg a ride that way.

clue.text: Wild lad married Vanessa

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so the letters run riot into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An unruly young man has wed a woman named Vanessa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges LAD MARRIED. Vanessa looks like a woman's name but is the butterfly genus.
explanation.definitionFit: This butterfly belongs to the genus Vanessa, so the genus name stands for one of its species.

clue.text: Sanctuary given to sacred writing by pauper

parts.note: a haven is a place of refuge or sanctuary
OT abbreviates the Old Testament, a body of sacred scripture

explanation.surface: A refuge is granted to holy scripture by a poor person.
explanation.definitionFit: A person without wealth, the opposite of one of the haves, is a poor person or pauper.

clue.text: Finish one without speaking

indicators.note: speaking means the word is heard rather than read, giving a same-sounding spelling

parts.note: someone who goes without something is a lacker, one who lacks

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get a job done in silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without speaking' looks like 'silently', but 'speaking' points to a word said aloud: LACKER, one who lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy varnish applied as the final coat is a finish for wood or metal.

clue.text: Fail to engage gear shift

definitions.meaning: a worn clutch is said to ... when it does not grip and the gear does not take
a shift is a simple loose dress or undergarment, the same as a petticoat

explanation.definitionFit: A clutch that slips fails to engage, and a shift is a loose undergarment of the same name.

clue.text: Trace wrong farmer, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this says the phrase is heard, giving the same sound with a different spelling

parts.note: a wrong is a sin and a farmer tills, so a farmer of wrong is a sin tiller

explanation.surface: A hint suggests a farmer has erred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the sound of it' turns SIN TILLER, one who tills wrongdoing, into the word heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount or the slightest spark of something, as in not a hint of evidence.

clue.text: Tackle tea theme -ridiculous solution offered by Queen

indicators.note: absurd and laughable, so these letters are scrambled into nonsense and back into sense

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a silly tea-party theme, with royal advice to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculous' rearranges TACKLE TEA THEME. The queen is Marie Antoinette, credited (doubtfully) with the remark about starving peasants.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Antoinette is said to have offered this as the remedy for peasants who had no bread.

clue.text: Badger, a despicable creature

definitions.meaning: to badger is to pester or harass someone persistently
a contemptible man, a cad or rotter

explanation.definitionFit: To pursue relentlessly like a dog on a trail; also an old term for a contemptible man.

clue.text: Pick on two boys — one's English

parts.note: Vic is a short form of the boy's name Victor
Tim is a short form of the boy's name Timothy, the second of the pair
one is I, so one's is I'S, written IS

explanation.surface: A pair of lads gang up on someone, one of them English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two boys' supplies two names in a row, VIC and TIM; 'one's' reads as I'S.
explanation.definitionFit: To single someone out for unfair treatment is to pick on them.

clue.text: Liberal — I had come upon one with intelligence, with excessive desire

parts.note: I had contracts to I'D
one is the Roman numeral I
nous is common sense or practical intelligence

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician claims to have met someone clever who was lustful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come upon' and 'with' are positional links in this across answer, each joining the next piece on after the last.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustful, given to strong sexual desire, from the Latin for desire, libido.

clue.text: Don't alter singular festival in Asia

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
Tet is the Vietnamese lunar New Year festival

explanation.surface: A request to leave an Asian festival unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for let it stand: a proofreader's instruction to keep the text as it was.

clue.text: When killing is permitted, offshore area is further forward

parts.note: the open sea is the expanse of water away from the coast
is contracts to 'S
on means onward, further forward, as in move on

explanation.surface: The killing season starts when a stretch of sea moves ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: The time of year when hunting a given game animal is legally allowed.

clue.text: Pragmatist gives sappers a set of tasks

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are sappers, are abbreviated RE
a to-do list is a set of tasks

explanation.surface: A practical officer hands the army engineers their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are military engineers; the British Army's are the Royal Engineers, RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who accepts things as they are and deals with them practically is a pragmatist.

clue.text: Reptile I considered supplied with air

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake, a reptile
to rate something is to consider or judge it

explanation.surface: A snake's owner thinks it needs fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that takes in air naturally is aspirated, and breath-filled sounds are too.

clue.text: Check on seeds

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in letters
pulses are the edible seeds of legumes such as lentils

explanation.surface: Someone inspects the seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive back or halt an attack is to check it.

clue.text: Canvas covers feel bad

parts.note: tops are lids, things that cover
to ail is to be unwell

explanation.surface: Tarpaulin covers make someone feel sick.
explanation.definitionFit: A sail set above the lowest on a mast is a piece of canvas, as sailcloth is called.

clue.text: Wash fine material, say, bringing up colour

indicators.note: say means the fabric word is heard, so its sound is written another way

parts.note: lawn is a fine linen or cotton fabric

indicators.note: in a down answer bringing up means the colour word is written from the bottom upward

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: Someone washes delicate cloth, and the colour runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives LAUN for LAWN; 'bringing up' turns RED into DER.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash and iron clothes, now also to pass dirty money through clean accounts.

clue.text: Stock a range of goods with time

parts.note: a product line is a range of goods
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper stocks a product range, given time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry or descent, as in coming from good stock.

clue.text: Mouth opens, letting in pea soup — your new cuisine

indicators.note: the openings of the seven words are taken, each word's first letter

explanation.surface: Someone opens wide to gobble pea soup in the modern style of cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opens' takes the first letters of the seven words after it. 'Mouth' is a verb here, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To lip-synch is to mouth the words of a recorded song without singing.

clue.text: Standard answer to first question of catechism

definitions.meaning: a usual pattern or expected level

definitions.text: answer to first question of catechism
definitions.meaning: the Book of Common Prayer catechism asks your name and prints ... as the reply

explanation.walkthrough: The Church of England catechism opens 'What is your Name?' and gives the reply as 'N. or M.', blanks for the child's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is a standard; the prayer book prints the reply to What is your Name? as N or M.

clue.text: Lithe fellows beginning to take something to remedy a deficiency

parts.note: lithe means supple, bending easily
fellows are men

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word, its first letter, is taken

explanation.surface: Agile men start on a dietary pill to make up for something missing.
explanation.definitionFit: An addition, such as a vitamin pill, that makes up for something lacking.

clue.text: Keen to entertain lavishly, turning up a pound short

indicators.note: short of a pound means that letter goes missing from the word
in a down answer turning up means the word is written from the bottom upward

parts.note: to regale guests is to entertain them lavishly
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from libra

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to throw a lavish party but is a pound short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' gives ELAGER; 'short' removes L for the pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager and keen are synonyms for being enthusiastic and impatient for something.

clue.text: Where servicemen eat sloppy food

definitions.meaning: the dining hall for officers or other ranks in the forces
an unappetising, soft dish, a dog's dinner

explanation.definitionFit: The forces' dining hall shares its name with an unappetising, sloppy dish of food.

clue.text: Tardy? Late? Wrong! Up-to-date!

indicators.note: wrong means not right, so these letters are put out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A string of exclamations about someone late, called out as modern.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern, belonging to recent times, as in a latter-day saint.

clue.text: Letter American servicemen returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the whole pair of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: GIs are US soldiers

explanation.surface: Some US soldiers sent back a letter home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns both pieces around as one run, so the soldiers' letters lead the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighteenth character of the Greek alphabet, so a letter.

clue.text: NHS employee worked as sir instructed

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A health-service worker did exactly as a senior doctor told them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges SIR INSTRUCTED; 'as' just links. The NHS is Britain's National Health Service, and senior surgeons are addressed as sir.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse who visits patients at home in a local area is employed by the health service.
